veranderings.blok: Party plekke is nat en party is droog
veranderings.voor: Reën val nie oral op die aarde dieselfde hoeveelheid nie.
veranderings.na: Daar val nie oral op die aarde ewe veel reën nie.
veranderings.rede: 'Reën val dieselfde hoeveelheid' is a wooden construction; 'daar val ewe veel reën' is the natural Afrikaans form with the same meaning.

veranderings.blok: Party plekke is nat en party is droog
veranderings.rede: 'een enkele jaar' echoes English 'a single year'; 'in een jaar' says the same and still contrasts with 'in 'n hele jaar'.

veranderings.voor: 'n Mens kan reën meet en die maat daarvoor is millimeter.
veranderings.na: 'n Mens kan reën meet, en die maat daarvoor is millimeter.
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two sentences with their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
'n millimeter hoog met water bedek' is awkward; 'met 'n millimeter water bedek' is the natural phrasing and leaves the protected 'n plat oppervlak' intact.
'saam' is vague here; 'bymekaargetel' says clearly that the millimetres are added up.
'daardie plek' points back to a place that the block never names.
Three sentences in a row open with 'Die kaart'; a pronoun here improves the flow and the reference stays clear.
With a countable noun after 'soorte', Afrikaans normally uses the plural ('twee soorte kaarte'); this is the block heading, not the lesson title.

veranderings.voor: hoe warm plekke is en 'n reënvalkaart
veranderings.na: hoe warm plekke is, en 'n reënvalkaart
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two sentences with their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.
In this kind of clause Afrikaans normally uses the existential 'daar' ('hoeveel reën daar val').

veranderings.voor: lees elke skakering in sy eie sleutel op
veranderings.na: kyk in elke kaart se eie sleutel wat die skakering beteken
veranderings.rede: 'oplees' means to read aloud, and 'sy' could refer to the shade rather than the map; the new wording says what the learner does and whose key it is.

veranderings.voor: dat warm nie ook nat beteken nie
veranderings.na: dat 'n warm plek nie noodwendig nat is nie
veranderings.rede: Read literally, 'warm beteken nie ook nat nie' says warm never means wet, which the Amazon example in the same block contradicts; the intended point is that warm does not imply wet.

veranderings.voor: Lees Suid-Afrika self op die reënvalkaart af
veranderings.na: Kyk na Suid-Afrika self op die reënvalkaart
veranderings.rede: You read values off a map, not a country; 'kyk na Suid-Afrika' is the natural phrasing.
'in 'n skakering staan' is unidiomatic; a part of a map 'het' a shade.

veranderings.voor: Hoeveel reën op 'n plek val en in millimeter gemeet word.
veranderings.na: Die hoeveelheid reën wat op 'n plek val, gemeet in millimeter.
veranderings.rede: In the current definition the subject of 'gemeet word' is unclear; the new form says plainly that the amount is measured in millimetres. If this definition is shared across lessons, it should go to the writer.

vlae.blok: Party plekke is nat en party is droog
vlae.teks: Die Amasone in Suid-Amerika is een van daardie baie nat plekke.
vlae.rede: 'Die Amasone' on its own usually means the river; the lesson means the region or rainforest (also in 'Twee soorte kaart langs mekaar'). It is not changed because the intended term, and whether it matches the video or other lessons, is a content decision.
